html:
The Flemish Movement is the long campaign by the Dutch-speaking Flemings of northern Belgium for the rights of their language and, later, self-rule.

When Belgium was founded in the Belgian Revolution, French was the language of government, courts, army and higher education, though most Belgians spoke Dutch dialects. The movement won Dutch in the courts and schools from the 1870s, and the University of Ghent began teaching in Dutch in 1930. Some radicals worked with the German occupiers in both world wars, which stained the movement.

In the 1960s the language border was fixed by law, and quarrels led to the splitting of the University of Leuven in 1968. From 1970 a series of reforms turned Belgium into a federal state, with Flemish, Walloon and Brussels regions and language communities. The Golden Spurs are its symbol.
sum: The Flemish Movement is the long campaign by the Dutch-speaking Flemings of northern Belgium for the rights of their language and, later, self-rule.
